outline.chapter_title: Why 1-bit LLMs: Motivation, Challenges, and the Promise of BitNet b1.58
outline.description: Introduce the motivation for ultra-low-bit Large Language Models, the environmental and economic pressures of scaling, and how BitNet b1.58 frames a new era where ternary-weight Transformers can match full-precision performance while drastically reducing cost.
subtopics: The compute and energy footprint of modern LLMs
Limits of conventional scaling: memory bandwidth and power
Post-training quantization vs. architectural rethinking
Contributions of BitNet b1.58: ternary weights, 8-bit activations, FP16-level quality
Overview of key results: speed, memory, energy, and throughput gains
A new scaling law linking performance to cost for 1.58-bit LLMs

outline.chapter_title: Background: Transformers, Inference Cost, and Quantization Basics
outline.description: Build the necessary foundations in Transformer computation and quantization, focusing on where cost arises (matrix multiplications, memory movement) and how lower precision affects accuracy and efficiency.
subtopics: Transformer internals: attention, MLPs, and the dominance of linear layers
Inference bottlenecks: FLOPs, memory access, latency, and bandwidth
Quantization primer: weights vs. activations, symmetric vs. asymmetric, zero-point
Post-training quantization landscape: SmoothQuant, GPTQ, AWQ, QuIP and trade-offs
Quantization-aware training vs. train-from-scratch low-bit models
Why 1–2 bit arithmetic promises orders-of-magnitude energy savings

outline.chapter_title: From 16-bit to Ternary: The Evolution from BitNet to BitNet b1.58
outline.description: Explain the trajectory from 16-bit floating-point LLMs to 1-bit and ternary-weight architectures, highlighting why adding zero creates a strong modeling advantage.
subtopics: BitNet concept: replacing floating-point multiplications with integer additions
Binary vs. ternary weights: why introducing zero matters
Information content: why log2(3) ≈ 1.58 bits
Feature filtering via zero weights and sparsity effects
Comparing modeling capacity: binary vs. ternary under similar training

outline.description: Detail the Transformer architecture used in BitNet b1.58 and its LLaMA-like components that ensure compatibility and performance.
subtopics: BitLinear in place of nn.Linear: what changes and why
Weights at 1.58 bits (ternary), activations at 8 bits
RMSNorm, SwiGLU, rotary positional embeddings, and bias removal
Keeping embeddings in full precision and why that matters
Compatibility with open-source stacks: Hugging Face, vLLM, llama.cpp
Training from scratch paradigm for low-bit LLMs

outline.description: Dive into the exact quantization functions and practical details, emphasizing simplicity, symmetry, and per-token activation scaling.
subtopics: Absmean scaling: gamma = mean(|W|) and its intuition
RoundClip operator to map to {-1, 0, +1}
Symmetric activation quantization to [-Qb, Qb] per token (no zero-point)
Practical effects of symmetric activations on implementation and accuracy
Per-matrix vs. per-channel scaling considerations
Training considerations: gradient-through-quantization (e.g., straight-through estimator) and stability

outline.chapter_title: A New Computation Paradigm: Integer Additions Replace Floating-Point Multiplications
outline.description: Explain how ternary-weight matrix multiplications are implemented and why they dramatically reduce energy consumption and latency.
subtopics: Matrix multiply with ternary weights: coding multiplies as adds and sign operations
Arithmetic intensity vs. memory movement for low-bit kernels
Energy model intuition: FP16 add/mul vs. INT8 add
Memory hierarchy: DRAM to SRAM transfers dominate at scale
Why power limits dominate chip performance and how 1.58-bit helps
Kernel support: Ladder 2-bit kernels and integration in FasterTransformer

outline.description: Detail the training and evaluation configuration to enable fair comparisons against FP16 LLaMA-like baselines.
subtopics: Pretraining data: RedPajama 100B tokens
Model scales: 3B, 3.9B, 7B, 13B, 70B
Perplexity benchmarks: WikiText2, C4
Zero-shot end tasks: ARC (Easy/Challenge), HellaSwag, Winogrande, PIQA, OpenBookQA, BoolQ
Measurement methodology: time per output token, memory footprint
Implementation stack: FasterTransformer with 2-bit kernels, GPU environment

outline.chapter_title: Results: Accuracy, Perplexity, and Pareto Improvements
outline.description: Present and interpret core findings: BitNet b1.58 matches or exceeds FP16 performance starting from 3B while achieving large latency and memory reductions.
subtopics: Perplexity parity with FP16 from 3B scale
Zero-shot task performance narrowing gap with scale
3.9B BitNet b1.58 surpassing FP16 3B at lower cost
Pareto frontier shift: accuracy vs. latency/memory
Implications for model selection at deployment time

outline.chapter_title: Systems Gains: Latency, Memory, Energy, and Throughput at Scale
outline.description: Analyze system-level benefits as model size increases, including quantified speedups and energy savings, and how they compound with scale.
subtopics: Latency trends: up to 4.1x faster at 70B vs. FP16 baseline
Memory trends: growing benefits as embeddings’ proportion shrinks
Energy estimates: 71.4x arithmetic energy savings for matmul on 7nm
End-to-end energy with longer sequences and larger models
Throughput on two A100 80GB with pipeline parallelism: 11x batch, 8.9x tokens/sec
Kernel and compiler opportunities beyond current 2-bit kernels

outline.chapter_title: A New Scaling Law: Re-thinking Model Size vs. Cost with 1.58-bit LLMs
outline.description: Formalize the emerging scaling relation between performance and cost for ternary-weight LLMs and provide practical equivalences for capacity planning.
subtopics: Why low-bit changes the performance–cost frontier
Empirical equivalences: 13B (1.58-bit) vs. 3B (FP16), 30B vs. 7B, 70B vs. 13B
Interpreting speed, memory, and energy as co-equal design axes
Budgeting for deployment: batch size, sequence length, and KV cache
When to choose 1.58-bit models over smaller FP16 baselines

outline.chapter_title: Training at Token Scale and Generalization
outline.description: Report results from training with 2 trillion tokens and compare with state-of-the-art 3B models, highlighting generalization benefits.
subtopics: 2T-token training following StableLM-3B data recipe
Tasks: Winogrande, PIQA, SciQ, LAMBADA, ARC-easy
Empirical gains over StableLM-3B across tasks
Token scaling effects for ternary-weight models
Stability and optimization considerations at long training horizons

outline.description: Discuss broader impacts, practical deployment scenarios, and research directions enabled by 1.58-bit LLMs.
subtopics: MoE with 1.58-bit: reducing memory and inter-chip communication
Long-context inference: 8-bit activations and potential 4-bit KV caches
Edge and mobile deployment: CPU-friendliness and on-device LLMs
Specialized hardware opportunities (e.g., LPUs) for 1–2 bit arithmetic
Software ecosystem: serving stacks, compilers, and kernel libraries
Open challenges: quantizer design, activation precision, robustness, and evaluation
